target_customer: Telehealth companies and medical practices needing insurance verification and routine phone work
problem: Verifying patient insurance benefits and handling routine non-clinical phone calls is manual, slow and costly for providers.
product_category: Healthcare administration AI (insurance verification, voice agents)

founders.name: Sherwood Callaway
founders.background_notes: 2x YC founder; 10+ years infrastructure/DevOps per YC page

exit.reason: Reported acqui-hire by 11x; the founder announced that the Opkit platform would be wound down over the following months. Price undisclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Insurance eligibility verification required payer and clearinghouse integrations and HIPAA compliance; the later voice-AI pivot (2024) was standard LLM-era engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and compliance (HIPAA, SOC 2) gave some friction but no data or network moat; many voice-AI entrants appeared by 2024.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Clearinghouses and EHR tools served traditional providers (2023 launch coverage); no incumbent copied or bought Opkit. The team was acqui-hired by 11x in Nov 2024 per directory profiles and the platform was wound down.

market_need_then: At launch in March 2023 coverage cited telehealth adoption and large US insurance billing administration spend (Rock Health, McKinsey, Center for American Progress figures per AlleyWatch).

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found nothing about Opkit's name, logo or community; it appears only in launch press and directories. No evidence the brand drove growth.

pivots.to: Generative-AI back-office call center for medical practices (human in the loop)

outcome_analysis: Opkit joined YC in S21, launched an insurance-verification product for telehealth firms in March 2023 with a roughly $1M seed, and in August 2024 pivoted to a generative-AI back-office call center for medical practices. It never announced a Series A. In November 2024 directory profiles (CB Insights and others) report an acqui-hire by 11x, and the founder's own post is reported to say the platform would be wound down. No cause is stated by the founders in the sources I could open, so the failure factors are inferred from the timeline: about 18 months after launch and no follow-on round, followed by a team-only exit.
notes: Searches done: outcome, funding, funding cross-check (launch coverage), competitor, branding. The 11x acquisition (Nov 2024) rests on directory profiles (CB Insights, dead-startups, bouncewatch) and a search summary of the founder's LinkedIn post; no 11x press release or primary source was opened, and the YC page text does not mention it, so the date and acqui-hire framing are medium confidence. Directory status Inactive is consistent. Seed amount ($1M, March 2023) and investors agree across AlleyWatch, MobiHealthNews and Axios headlines; one aggregator lists a separate $125K round on 2021-08-31 and Greylock appears only in the AlleyWatch interview; the $125K figure is unverified and not recorded. The YC deal is not recorded as a round. Competitors: launch coverage dates from 2023-03 (names Availity, Candid Health via CB Insights comparisons, ZocDoc) not from the S21 batch, so none are listed; the company founded 2021 and launched publicly only in 2023. Branding search returned nothing relevant. Sites axios/crowdfundinsider returned 403 and were not worked around. Status conflict: the directory says Inactive while exit.type is acquisition; I kept acquisition because several profiles (CB Insights, dead-startups, bouncewatch) report it, and Inactive is consistent with the platform wind-down. The merge warning on this is expected.
